lesson.title: Individual criminal-risk assessment
lesson.summary: Distinguish individual criminal-risk prediction from support of human assessment already based on linked facts.

prerequisites.reason: The ban expressly turns on prediction solely based on profiling or personality assessment.
The learner must distinguish the criminal-risk elements from a general law-enforcement label.

blocks: The **criminal-risk ban** concerns AI risk assessment predicting whether a natural person will commit a criminal offence, based solely on personal profiling or assessment of personality traits and characteristics.
Identify the predicted event, person and basis. A tool's output being called 'risk intelligence' does not resolve those elements.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 5(1)(d); Annex III 6

blocks: The point provides a boundary for AI supporting human assessment of involvement in criminal activity already based on objective, verifiable facts directly linked to criminal activity.
The **factual-human-support boundary** is not satisfied by adding a person after a purely trait-based prediction. The existing human assessment and linked facts must be shown.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 5(1)(d); Annex III 6

blocks: Fictional Northbridge clinic: a system predicts offending solely from personality traits. A human signs the flag without a pre-existing linked factual assessment. Those facts do not establish the support boundary.

Changed case: a human assessment of involvement already rests on specified objective/verifiable facts directly linked to criminal activity, and the AI supports it. Examine that boundary and other law separately; it is not blanket permission for any later use.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 5(1)(d); Annex III 6

blocks: Keep Article 5 distinct from Annex III enforcement classification. A permitted support function may still require high-risk analysis. A prohibited trait-based function cannot be authorised by an Annex III listing.
Record the facts, their direct link, human assessment's timing and the actual support function. Do not invent criminal suspicion from a demographic or personality correlation.

sources.title: AI Act, 27 July 2026 baseline: Article 5(1)(d); Annex III 6
